title: Design tokens as CSS custom properties
when: The user wants a token file or a small design system: named values for color, type, space, radius, shadow and motion.
inputs: existing palette and scales, if any
prompt:
Goal: A tokens.css with a primitive tier and a semantic tier that every other rule reads, so a retheme edits one file.
Steps:
1. Tier 1, primitives with neutral names: --blue-600: #1d4ed8; --gray-900: #111827; --size-4: 1rem; --radius-2: 6px.
2. Tier 2, semantic aliases naming the role: --color-text: var(--gray-900); --color-action: var(--blue-600); --space-card: var(--size-5).
3. Components read only semantic tokens; a component knob gets a local property with fallback: .btn { background: var(--btn-bg, var(--color-action)) }.
4. Name as category, role, variant, state: --color-action-hover, --color-border-subtle; no look based names (--light-blue) in tier 2.
5. Group the file by category with a comment header each and keep it under about 80 tokens.
6. Link tokens.css before style.css with a relative path.
Quality bar:
- No raw hex, px spacing or shadow outside tokens.css.
- Every semantic token resolves to a primitive.
- Names read clearly in the inspector.
Pitfalls:
- One flat tier, so a theme change means renaming everything.
- Hundreds of unused tokens.
- Tokens used as media query breakpoints, which does not work.
Verify:
- [ ] tokens.css defines both tiers on :root.
- [ ] style.css uses var() for colors and sizes.
- [ ] Component fallbacks exist.
- [ ] tokens.css loads first.
Output: tokens.css with both tiers and the stylesheet updated to read from it.

examples.input: crie um arquivo de design tokens para o projeto
examples.output: tokens.css: primitives blue-50..900, gray, size-1..9; semantic color-text, color-action, space-card
